name: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
title: Blockchain to Ledger Reconciliation
answer: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transaction records with internal accounting ledgers for digital assets. It covers wallet balances, transaction hashes, fees, token transfers, smart contract events, and fiat valuations. The scope includes detecting missing, duplicate, or mispriced entries across exchanges, custodians, and self-hosted wallets. It also spans periodic close, audit support, and tax basis tracking.

crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

sections.body: Blockchain to ledger reconciliation is the process of matching on-chain transaction records with internal accounting ledgers for digital assets. It covers wallet balances, transaction hashes, fees, token transfers, smart contract events, and fiat valuations. The scope includes detecting missing, duplicate, or mispriced entries across exchanges, custodians, and self-hosted wallets. It also spans periodic close, audit support, and tax basis tracking.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work typically runs on a data pipeline that pulls from blockchain nodes or indexers, exchange APIs, and the general ledger or ERP. It uses a normalized data store for addresses, transaction metadata, and accounting entries. Compute is usually cloud-based, with scheduled batch jobs or event-driven triggers. Some setups use an orchestration layer to sequence extraction, transformation, and matching.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Reconciliation starts by extracting native blockchain transactions and internal ledger postings into a common schema. Matching rules then pair entries by transaction hash, wallet address, asset, amount, and timestamp, with tolerance for timing differences and fee handling. Unmatched items are flagged for review, and adjustments are posted only after approval. Automated exception reports group breaks by type, such as missing deposit, duplicate withdrawal, or valuation difference.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: The main risks are incomplete data, incorrect valuation, and unauthorized access to private keys or exchange credentials. Access to reconciliation tools is usually role-based, with separation between those who post journal entries and those who approve adjustments. Provenance requires retaining source transaction IDs, block heights, and API call logs so every reconciled line can be traced back to an on-chain record. Audit trails should show who changed a match rule or manually cleared an exception.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Reconciliation is moving toward continuous, near real-time matching rather than month-end batch runs. More firms are adopting standardized data models for digital assets so that wallets, exchanges, and ledgers can be compared without custom mapping each time. Machine learning is being used to suggest likely matches for unmatched items and to learn recurring exception patterns, but human review remains the final control. Expect closer integration with proof-of-reserves and regulatory reporting as digital asset accounting matures.
